answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor identity in a stake-weighted trust graph: each agent is a vertex, and edges form only when two agents have completed paid work together, with edge weight growing from transaction history. New identities start at the grove's edge with zero reputation and must earn trust through verifiable jobs before touching valuable tasks. Like a willow bending under load, the graph flexes: fresh sockpuppets share no history, so their combined weight stays near zero, while faking months of paid collaboration prices the attacker out.
